name: spring-switch
title: Springy switches
summary: Two settings switches whose thumbs spring across with a little overshoot (a graphicsLayer translationX over an animated progress, at paint time) while the blue track fades in with the same progress.
prompt: A settings card with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth switches; tapping a row flips its switch with a springy thumb that slightly overshoots and a track colour that fades between grey and blue.
teaches: Animate a state change at paint time: a root variable {"value": "@on", "anim": 0.3} eases from 0 to 1 whenever @on flips, and every visual reads it
Give the thumb a spring feel with an expression over that progress: x = 22 * (p + 0.5 * sin(pi * p) * (2 * @on - 1)) overshoots about 10% and settles, in graphicsLayer translationX (no layout runs)
Cross-fade the track colour by stacking an 'on' layer whose graphicsLayer alpha is the same progress
pitfalls: JSON has no colour expression: fade between colours with an overlay's alpha

A {value, anim} animation has only the standard cubic easing; an overshoot is an expression over the eased progress, and the sine term flips sign with the target, so a tap during the 0.3 s travel jumps the thumb by up to 2 dp

Do not move the thumb with a layout dimension and an OVERSHOOT animationSpec: Java re-measures a width bound to a variable, but its bounds animation stops at the first frame the eased progress reaches 1, so an overshooting easing leaves the thumb at the overshoot (about 2 dp past the end) until the next layout (U, see EXAMPLES_FINDINGS)
Weights ignore spacedBy (U3): the text column takes weight 1 and the switch sits after it with no spacedBy

snippets.note: thumb translationX: 22 * (p + 0.5 sin(pi p)(2 @bt - 1)), the overshoot

check.describe: Wi-Fi on, Bluetooth off. A tap on the Bluetooth row at 0.1 s, captured 0.08 s later: its thumb is past the middle and the track half blue. Settled after 0.6 s. Resized (narrow 240, wide 540) the rows fill the width with the switches pinned right; a switch keeps its 52 dp track, so its 22 dp thumb travel is a fixed distance by design.
